obligation: FTC Act Section 5 (unfair or deceptive acts or practices)
basis: A for-profit software publisher in interstate commerce, outside the statutory carve-outs, with no size threshold. Both theories apply: reasonable security for the end-consumer data it holds, and truthful public, contractual and questionnaire statements

obligation: COPPA Rule
basis: The service is sold to businesses and is not directed to children under 13

obligation: CCPA/CPRA and CPPA regulations
citation: Cal. Civ. Code 1798.100 et seq.; Cal. Code Regs. tit. 11, 7000 et seq.
applies: Yes (business for own data; service provider for customer data). Cybersecurity audit trigger open
basis: Revenue over the $26,625,000 threshold and business in California, so a business for its own data (about 70,000 California consumers); a service provider under DPAs for about 11 million California end consumers. Whether service-provider processing counts toward the cybersecurity audit threshold is open, decision due 2026-12-31

obligation: DOJ Data Security Program
applies: Yes (applicability check; no covered data transactions identified)
basis: Holds bulk U.S. personal identifiers and personal health data above the thresholds; hosting and the 14 sub-processors are in the United States; the contractor in Poland has no customer data access

obligation: Protecting Americans' Data from Foreign Adversaries Act (PADFA)
basis: The company processes customer data under DPAs to provide the service and does not sell or transfer it as a data broker

obligation: FCC CPNI rules
basis: The product has no voice service; the company is not a carrier or interconnected VoIP provider

obligation: FedRAMP
basis: No federal agency customers

obligation: SEC public-company cybersecurity disclosure
basis: The company is privately held

obligation: HIPAA Security Rule, as a business associate
basis: The company creates, receives, maintains and transmits ePHI for 46 covered entities under BAAs, so it is a business associate (45 CFR 160.103) and the Security Rule applies (164.302). No size exemption; 164.306(b) affects how, not whether

obligation: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule, business associate duties
basis: Notice to the covered entity no later than 60 days after discovery (164.410); the BAAs shorten this to 10 business days

obligation: HIPAA Security Rule NPRM (2025)
basis: Not a final rule; tracked for planning

obligation: FTC Health Breach Notification Rule
basis: 16 CFR 318.1 excludes HIPAA business associates acting as such; PHI is handled under the BAAs

obligation: Computer-Security Incident Notification Rule: bank service provider notice
basis: Whether the platform is a covered service under the Bank Service Company Act is a legal judgment; counsel treats it as covered, and the bank contracts require notice of incidents that disrupt services for 4 or more hours in any case

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act
basis: A third-party agent for Florida personal information it holds for customers (about 6 million Florida end-consumer records; 501.171(6)(a)); a covered entity for its own data

obligation: Breach notification laws of other states
citation: Each state where affected individuals reside (for example Cal. Civ. Code 1798.82(b))
basis: End consumers are in all 50 states; service-provider duties run to customers for customer data, and resident notices apply to company-owned data

obligation: Florida interception law: all-party consent to record calls
basis: The call summarizer (AI-005) records sales and support calls; counsel applies the all-party rule to every call

obligation: Customer contract commitments (MSA, DPA, BAA)
citation: Customer MSA, DPA and BAA templates
basis: Availability of 99.9% and 99.95% with credits; incident notice within 48 hours (24 hours for 38 Enterprise customers); BAA notice within 10 business days; 30-day sub-processor notice; deletion within 30 days; no AI training; U.S. hosting

obligation: Customer requirement for a SOC 2 Type 2 report
basis: The MSA promises a current SOC 2 Type 2 report under NDA; the current report covers Security and Availability

obligation: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard
basis: The company bills through a payment processor and does not accept card data in the product; card numbers pasted into tickets are redacted by default

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports (pending rule)
basis: No final rule; P08 rechecks the covered-entity criteria when it is final

obligation: OFAC sanctions risk for ransomware payments
basis: Applies to all U.S. persons, with strict liability

obligation: Colorado SB26-189 (AI in consequential decisions)
applies: No (not triggered while no AI feature makes consequential decisions)
basis: AI Assist drafts replies that agents send, Answer Bot answers questions and takes no account actions, and triage routes tickets
